startups.name: NimbusForge
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: ran a permanent unpaid 'trial week', then withheld final paychecks from contractors.

reasons.claim: Unpaid 'trial weeks' used as free labor
reasons.detail: Sample scenario showing the data shape. Candidates were asked to complete a full week of production work unpaid before an offer that rarely materialized.
Demonstrates how a 'pay' verdict is justified with documentation in a real entry.

startups.name: PayLoop
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: dark-pattern billing that makes cancellation nearly impossible and keeps charging after 'cancel'.

reasons.detail: Sample: the cancel button is hidden behind a support-ticket queue with multi-day SLAs, while billing continues monthly.

startups.name: HustlrHQ
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: '90-hour weeks are the minimum' culture with rapid burnout and high first-year attrition.

reasons.detail: Sample scenario: weekend work expected by default; PTO discouraged in practice.

startups.name: DataKraken
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: quietly resold customer data and suffered an unreported breach.

reasons.claim: Customer data resold to third parties
reasons.detail: Sample: usage telemetry sold to data brokers without meaningful consent.

startups.name: Brightwave Labs
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: 'AI' product is mostly manual offshore labor; outcomes and pricing are misrepresented.

reasons.detail: Sample: marketed as autonomous, actually a queue of human operators with unpredictable turnaround.
Sample illustrating overage charges that don't match the advertised model.

startups.name: Quotient Health
startups.summary: Illustrative sample entry: shut down overnight, stranding customers' paid annual plans and laying off staff without notice.

reasons.detail: Sample: annual subscribers lost access mid-term with no refunds issued.
Sample showing why all three verdicts can apply to one company.
